CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.cityofsanmarino.org
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone
Susan Jakubowski, Council Member  (626) 300-0709 Fax
Steve Talt, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber
Ken Ude, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Marcella Marlowe, Ph.D., City Manager  San Marino, CA 91108

  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 10, 2019 AT 6:00 P.M.
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the
Council with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
Adjourned Meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:00 a.m.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705 prior to the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL:  Council Member Jakubowski, Council Member Talt, Council
  Member Ude, Vice Mayor Shepherd Romey, and Mayor Huang.

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City
Hall, 2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and
the Recreation Department, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the
City’s website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council
by completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the
meeting. At this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – APRIL 10, 2019  PAGE 2 OF 5

the agenda. Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on
issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor
reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow
up on such items.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of
any upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without
having to read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance
on First Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not
require having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance
or resolution be read in its entirety before taking any action.

  CEREMONIAL

1.  DONATE LIFE PRESENTATION

2.  NATIONAL LIBRARY WEEK PRESENTATION

  CONSENT

3.  RECEIVE AND FILE DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR MARCH 2019

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council receive and file the disbursements
  report for the month of March 2019.

4.  RECEIVE AND FILE FINANCIAL REPORT AS OF FEBRUARY 28,
  2019

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council receive and file the financial report
  as of February 28, 2019.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council approve the minutes of the joint
  meeting with the Library Board of Trustees of March 13, 2019, the regular
  meeting of March 13, 2019, the special meeting of March 20, 2019, the special
  meeting of March 27, 2019, and the adjourned meeting of March 29, 2019.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – APRIL 10, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 5

  TREASURER’S REPORT

6.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF
  FEBRUARY 2019

  Recommendation: It is recommended that this report be received and filed.

  CONTINUED BUSINESS

7.  ADOPTION OF REVISIONS TO THE OCTOBER 2018 STREET
  TREE POLICY TO INCORPORATE CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL OF
  STREET TREE REMOVALS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council 1) adopt revisions to the October
  26, 2018 street tree policy and procedures related to incorporating City Council
  approval of street trees into the permit approval process; and 2) appoint ____
  as the primary City Council tree liaison and ____ as City Council tree liaison
  alternate.

  NEW BUSINESS

8.  APPEAL  TO  CONTEST  DETERMINATION THAT  AN
  ESTABLISHED TREE HAS BEEN SEVERELY PRUNED  OR
  DAMAGED – 875 SUSSEX ROAD

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council uphold the decision
  of the Planning Commission.

9.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R-19-08 ADOPTING A LIST OF
  PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-20 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE
  ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council approve Resolution No. R-19-08
  adopting a list of fiscal year 2019-20 funded by SB 1 Road Maintenance and
  Rehabilitation Account Funds.

10.  AWARD OF A CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT FOR STREET
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM PROJECT NO. 18-9271 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $1,111,700 TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT OF
  CORONA
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – APRIL 10, 2019  PAGE 4 OF 5

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Council 1) approve the plans and
  specifications for the Street Rehabilitation Program Project No. 18-9271; 2)
  award a construction agreement to All American Asphalt of Corona for the
  Street Rehabilitation Program Project No. 18-9271 in an amount not-to-exceed
  $1,111,700; and 3) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director to approve
  contract change orders if warranted in a cumulative amount not-to-exceed
  $55,600.

11.  RECOMMENDATION FROM THE RECREATION COMMISSION
  REQUESTING AN APPROPRIATION OF $30,000 FOR RE-
  ENVISIONING RECREATION

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council appropriate an amount not-to-
  exceed $30,000 from the General Fund Reserves and transfer those funds into
  the Recreation Budget account no. 101-60-4150-0000 for Fiscal Year 18-19 for
  the purposes of securing appropriate expertise to assist the City Manager and/or
  Community Services Director to perform comprehensive recreation
  programming and re-envisioning survey services.

12.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. R-19-09, AMENDING
  APPLICATION  REQUIREMENTS  AND  DEVELOPMENT
  STANDARDS  FOR  WIRELESS  TELECOMMUNICATIONS
  FACILITIES IN THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY AND SMALL
  WIRELESS FACILITIES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends Council adopt Resolution No. R-19-09.

  PUBLIC HEARING

13.  APPEAL FOR MODIFICATION TO CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT
  CUP94-22 AND VARIANCE V96-15 2265 HUNTINGTON DRIVE,
  (KT ENTERPRISES/STARBUCKS)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that Council approve the modification to
  Conditional Use Permit CUP94-22 and approve Resolution R-19-06.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of
San Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda
will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington
Drive, San Marino, California 91108.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA – APRIL 10, 2019  PAGE 5 OF 5

COUNCIL REPORTS

This is an opportunity for members of the City Council to inform the public of any
meetings or conferences they may have attended.

CITY COUNCIL CALENDAR

Scheduling dates for future Council meetings.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino City Council will adjourn to FRIDAY, APRIL 26, 2019, AT 8:00
A.M. in the Barth Room at the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108.

Dated: April 5, 2019  AMANDA FOWLER
Posted: April 5, 2019  ACTING CITY CLERK
